rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: A PLAN COMES TO THE BUTTON IN ITS OPTIMIZED SHAPE, AND IS NEVER RESHAPED BY THE OWNER'S ASK.
rules.says: A plan reaches the owner's approval button in the optimized shape the seed prints and the plans page states (take-up that claims and runs alone and first; file steps partitioned by file run at once; one landing step; no background run; cost said; no walk against staging), never reshaped by the owner's ask.

rules.heading: A plan comes to the button in its optimized shape
rules.quote: the owner's ask never reshapes it.
rules.says: A plan is never reshaped by the owner's ask; a session takes the shape from the seed and the plans page, not from the ask.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: It binds the session's own turns as well as a plan's steps.
rules.says: The optimized-plan-shape procedure binds the session's own turns as well as the steps of a plan.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: THE PLAN CHECK REFUSES A TITLE, A PULL, A TIER AND A FILES LINE, AND THE CHECK OF A CALL PASSES IN PLAN MODE.
rules.says: A plan must not have a title holding a phrase third-person-check.mjs refuses, a step pulling the live clone beside or before a file-writing step, a Files line saying read only beside a write word, or (if new) a file last written below the top tier; in plan mode hook-dispatch.mjs --can <tool> <one argument> passes alone; refusal names which copy of the plan check ran.

rules.heading: The plan check refuses a title, a pull, a tier and a Files line
rules.quote: `plan-guard.mjs` faults, as faults of shape that set no latch,
rules.says: The plan check's refusals on title, pull, Files line and tier are faults of shape that set no latch, so a plan is corrected and re-presented rather than the session being held.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: EVERY REPLY ENDS WITH THE STATE LINE, AND A PAUSE ON THE OWNER IS NEVER WRITTEN AS NOTHING OPEN.
rules.says: Every reply ends with a state line (paused, pending what; running, what; or finished, nothing pending), a pause on the owner is never written as nothing open, and 'Open for you' lists decisions only.
rules.live_quote: Report what changed and what it means, in plain words, with the state at the end: finished, paused on what, or running what.
rules.missing: That a pause on the owner is never written as nothing open; that 'Open for you' holds decisions only; 'every reply' scope and the state-line wording 'finished, nothing pending'.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: AN OPEN CHOICE IS THE FIRST THING IN A REPLY, UNTIL IT IS ANSWERED.
rules.says: While a choice is unanswered, the numbered options with the recommendation first open the reply (after a stop declaration and at most one lead-in line) and the report goes beneath them, never the choice under a long report.
rules.enforcer: stop-guard.mjs (refuses a reply whose options carry the recommended marker anywhere else; finds a choice only by that marker)
rules.live_quote: Bring back to the owner only a choice that is the owner's, with the recommended option first.
rules.missing: That an unanswered choice is the first thing in the reply (after a stop declaration and at most one lead-in line), report beneath it, never the choice under a long report.

rules.heading: An open choice is the first thing in a reply
rules.quote: `stop-guard.mjs` refuses a reply whose options carry the recommended marker anywhere else; it finds a choice only by that marker.
rules.says: Every option set must carry the recommended marker on the recommended option, because the guard recognises a choice only by that marker, and a reply with the marked options anywhere but the opening is refused.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: THE WHOLE DOCTRINE IS READ AT EVERY SESSION START AND AFTER EVERY COMPACTION
rules.says: At every session start and after every compaction the session reads every line of DOCTRINE.md (never its section list or a summary) from the live clone's copy /root/.claude/hub/DOCTRINE.md, before anything but reading and the status; a resume owes the read only when the transcript does not already hold every line.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: AFTER A COMPACTION OR A RESUME THE PRINTS ARE BOUNDED, THE DOCTRINE IS NOT, AND THE OWNER'S MESSAGES ARE READ WHOLE FROM A FILE.
rules.says: After a compaction every doctrine line is due as at a startup; the start print of the owner's messages is the newest ten since the previous compaction with the count of the rest and the path of a scratchpad file holding all of them, which the session reads in full before anything but reading and the status.
rules.enforcer: recallGate in hook-dispatch.mjs (holds main thread to reading and the status, without latching, until Read results cover every line; holds nothing while the file does not exist; passes TaskStop); compact-recall.mjs

rules.heading: After a compaction or a resume the prints are bounded
rules.quote: A startup is unchanged: every line of the doctrine, every lesson title.
rules.says: At a startup the print is unchanged: every line of the doctrine and every lesson title (only a compaction or a resume bounds the prints).

rules.heading: After a compaction or a resume the prints are bounded
rules.quote: the line printed at SessionStart names the lines due; the print of the owner's messages is the newest ten since the previous compaction (or since the session's start where there was none), oldest first
rules.says: The SessionStart line names the doctrine lines due, and the owner-message print is the newest ten since the previous compaction (or session start), oldest first, with the count of the rest and the path of a file under the session scratchpad named for the compaction holding every message whole and in order.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: the file is a print of the session's own transcript for the session's own reading, and nothing copies it into a repository.
rules.says: The recall file of the owner's messages is for the session's own reading only and is never copied into a repository.

rules.heading: After a compaction or a resume the prints are bounded
rules.quote: After such a start `recallGate` in `hook-dispatch.mjs` holds the main thread to reading and the status, without latching,
rules.says: After such a start the main thread is held to reading and the status, without latching, until Read results covering every line of the recall file and returned after the start are in the transcript; no hold while the file does not exist; passes TaskStop.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: The compaction is then said: the dispatcher records it with its time, the first status after it prints the time in California time,
rules.says: After a compaction the first reply after it must have a first line saying a compaction happened and at what time (California time), which may share the line with a stop declaration and which a follow-up carrying it discharges.
rules.enforcer: stop-guard.mjs (refuses the first reply after the compaction lacking it); hook-dispatch.mjs records it and the status page carries it under its updated line

rules.heading: After a compaction or a resume the prints are bounded
rules.quote: the dispatcher records it with its time, the first status after it prints the time in California time, the status page carries it under its updated line
rules.says: A compaction is recorded with its time by the dispatcher; the first status after it prints that time in California time and the status page carries it under its updated line.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: The brief prints the lessons as a count and the folder's path, with the reason on its own line where it cannot read the start's marker.
rules.says: The session brief prints the lessons as a count and the folder's path, with the reason on its own line where it cannot read the start's marker, rather than every lesson title.

rules.heading: After a compaction or a resume the prints are bounded
rules.quote: the doctrine's share is paid on purpose now
rules.says: The cost of reading every line of the doctrine after a compaction is paid on purpose and is not to be trimmed to save context.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: ONLY `staging` AND `main` REACH A REMOTE, IN EVERY REPO.
rules.says: In every repository only staging and main may be pushed to a remote; what is refused is stated in the harness-branch item near the top of the list.
rules.live_quote: Only staging and main reach a remote.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: AskUserQuestion is permanently banned.
rules.says: The AskUserQuestion tool (the choice popup) is permanently banned.
rules.live_quote: The choice popup is never used.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: Verify a push by reading the remote, not by reading the push output.
rules.says: A push is verified by reading the remote, not the push output, because no range line in the output means nothing moved.
rules.live_quote: - **Verify with `git ls-remote --heads origin` before telling the owner anything landed.** The push output is a claim; the remote is the fact.
rules.missing: The statement that no range line in the push output means nothing moved.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: A PUSH IS NOT A RELEASE — check the DEPLOY for that exact SHA.
rules.says: After a push, check the deploy for that exact SHA before calling work shipped; a session adding a hard gate to a pipeline must look especially for its own work silently not arriving, even though the gate passed locally.
rules.live_quote: A push is not a release, and a green row for an earlier commit is not a run for this one. Every workflow run for that exact commit is read by name and reported as concluded, with its conclusion, or as still running.
rules.missing: The warning that a session adding a hard gate to a pipeline has added a new way for its own work to silently not arrive and is least likely to look because the gate passed locally.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: AND ITS SIBLING: A PUSH IS NOT A CI RUN.
rules.says: The question after a push is whether there is a CI run whose head SHA is this commit and what its log said, never whether the newest run is green (a missing run is an absence); dispatching the workflow by hand against the branch is the fallback, and the release is then said to be verified by that dispatch.
rules.live_quote: a green row for an earlier commit is not a run for this one. Every workflow run for that exact commit is read by name and reported as concluded, with its conclusion, or as still running.
rules.missing: That a missing run is an absence (nothing red because nothing ran); that dispatching the workflow by hand against the branch is the fallback; that the release is then said to be verified by that dispatch.

rules.heading: ## The rules that get broken anyway — read these before typing
rules.quote: The shape of three of these is the same: the record names routes that failed, not ends that are impossible.
rules.says: Do not offer a route the lessons record as failed, and do not read its failure as the end being out of reach; check before promising, not after.

rules.quote: The owner should not have to request these per repo; the owner has, repeatedly, and the asking was the evidence the doctrine was missing a rule. Build them because the app exists.
rules.says: Every app ships the listed baseline items without the owner asking per repo; they are built because the app exists.
rules.live_quote: The owner should not have to request these per repo; the owner has, repeatedly, and the asking was the evidence the doctrine was missing a rule. Build them because the app exists.

rules.heading: ## The baseline every app ships without being asked (Doctrine §7e, §7f)
rules.quote: An (i) control in the app's own chrome — not a tab, not a footer link —
rules.says: Every app has an (i) control in its own chrome carrying what the app is, is not, home-screen install for every platform named, what changed, data sources with terms, how to report a problem, and the accessibility statement and licence.
rules.live_quote: **An (i) control in the app's own chrome** — not a tab, not a footer link — carrying what the app IS, what it is NOT, how to install it on a home screen with every platform NAMED,

rules.says: First-run orientation must survive whatever the reader presses to begin and then live permanently behind the (i); moved there, never copied.
rules.live_quote: **First-run orientation that SURVIVES whatever the reader presses to begin**, and then lives permanently behind the (i). Move it there; never copy it.
